title: Gaggan Anand Opens First India Restaurant Raga in New Delhi
excerpt: Asia's top-ranked chef is opening a 42-seat fine dining restaurant on Janpath, bringing his progressive Indian cuisine home after a decade in Bangkok.
body:
• Chef Gaggan Anand is opening Raga, a 42-seat restaurant on Janpath in New Delhi — his first permanent restaurant in India.
  • The name combines the initials of co-founder and head chef Rydo Anton (RA) with Gaggan Anand (GA), and references the Hindi musical term.
  • Anand's Bangkok restaurant Gaggan has topped Asia's 50 Best Restaurants list for five consecutive years, most recently in March 2026.
  • Raga will feature two tasting menus with a target price point of ₹8,000, using locally sourced Indian produce for the first time in Anand's career.

Gaggan Anand, the most decorated Indian chef on the planet, is finally opening a restaurant in his home country. Raga, a 42-seat fine dining destination on Janpath in the heart of New Delhi, marks the Kolkata-born chef's first permanent establishment in India after more than a decade of redefining Indian cuisine from Bangkok.

The restaurant, expected to open this summer, sits on prime real estate near Rashtrapati Bhavan, flanked by government buildings, luxury hotels, and historic markets. It represents what Esquire India called "the most significant restaurant launch India has seen in a generation."

The Name Behind the Restaurant

Raga is a collaboration between Anand and his head chef and business partner of 10 years, Rydo Anton. The name fuses their initials — RA from Rydo Anton and GA from Gaggan Anand — while also referencing the Hindi musical term "raga," meaning a melodic framework in Indian classical music.

"The restaurant will stand independently, with its own originality. It will have playfulness, but, above all, it will have complete creative freedom."

— Gaggan Anand, chef and restaurateur

Anand revealed the plans in a conversation with food critic Vir Sanghvi on Culinary Culture, saying he wanted to bring his cooking home on his own terms. "I am ready for India," he said.

What to Expect

Raga will offer two tasting menus, and diners can expect some of Anand's greatest hits, including his legendary Yoghurt Explosion — a riff on the olive spherification he learned under Ferran Adrià at the iconic El Bulli in Spain, reimagined with Indian flavors. The dish, a single spoonful of yogurt laced with chaat masala and black salt that bursts in the mouth, has been on his menu since 2010 and remains his most famous creation.

Being based in India will allow Anand, for the first time, to work directly with local produce — a shift from his Bangkok operation where Indian ingredients had to be sourced internationally. He has targeted a price point of ₹8,000 per person, positioning Raga as accessible by global fine dining standards.

Anand has also mentioned plans for wedding catering through the Raga brand, a nod to India's massive wedding market.

Five-Time Asia's Best

Anand's Bangkok restaurant Gaggan claimed the top spot on the Asia's 50 Best Restaurants list for the fifth consecutive year at a ceremony in Seoul in March 2026. He also holds two Michelin stars and has been featured on Netflix's Chef's Table.

His culinary empire in Bangkok now includes the flagship Gaggan Anand restaurant, Ms Maria & Mr Singh, and a collaboration with Louis Vuitton at LV The Place Bangkok. But India has always been the missing piece.

"Why doesn't he have a restaurant in India?" has been the question trailing Anand for years. He had previously dismissed the idea, citing regulatory hurdles and the challenges of operating in the Indian market. His only previous presence in Delhi was a 20-day residency at Hyatt Regency in 2023.

A Homecoming for Indian Cuisine

Anand's return carries symbolic weight for India's fine dining scene. A Kolkata-bred Punjabi who found global fame abroad, he represents a generation of Indian chefs who had to leave the country to gain international recognition. Raga reverses that trajectory — bringing world-class progressive Indian cuisine back to Indian soil, sourced from Indian farms, and priced for Indian diners.

The restaurant is expected to draw food enthusiasts from across India and abroad, and could help position New Delhi as a serious destination on the global fine dining map alongside Bangkok, Singapore, and Tokyo.
nri_angle: Anand's homecoming resonates with the Indian diaspora, many of whom have followed his rise from Bangkok and can now experience his cooking on home soil during visits to India.
